issues.source_quote: Опять Тимофеев пробки пережег! - Товарищ Тимофеев, когда это кончится?
issues.translation_quote: Comrade Timofeev, when will this end?
issues.justification: Fine in itself, but the pun on 'кончится/кончатся' is missing the later echo; not a major issue. (Minor loss of the double-entendre in the exchange 'Сейчас заканчиваю'.)

issues.source_quote: Он же давно умер! - Кто умер? - Я не про Вас это говорю!
issues.translation_quote: He died ages ago! - Who died? - I'm not talking about you!
issues.justification: Acceptable, but the key joke in this scene about Zinaida's dismissive 'Who is this' is preserved; no issue. (Placeholder retained for accuracy only if needed.)

issues.source_quote: Шайбу, шайбу...
issues.translation_quote: We want a goal! A goal...
issues.justification: The crowd chants the hockey cry 'Puck! Puck!' (a famous Soviet chant) as a comic anachronism echoing 'Царя, царя'; the translation changes it to 'goal' and the added 'We want' alters the rhythm, though the joke mostly survives. Minor loss only.

issues.source_quote: Пейте смело! - Здрав будь, боярин!
issues.translation_quote: Good health to thee, boyar!
issues.justification: Ivan's archaic speech is rendered with thee/thou, but this is inconsistent with the rest of his speech, which at times is modern (see below), harming character voice.

issues.source_quote: Ну, пошли дела кой-как.
issues.translation_quote: Well, things are sort of moving.
issues.justification: Register inconsistency is minor, but 'sort of' is Americanized against British-flavoured text.

issues.source_quote: Это - кинорежиссер Якин! ... Это я удачно зашел! Граждане, храните деньги в сберегательной кассе!
issues.translation_quote: Keep your savings in the State Savings Bank!
issues.justification: The Soviet slogan is rendered adequately, but 'State Savings Bank' adds explanation; minor at most.

issues.source_quote: Не закрывайте рот!
issues.translation_quote: Don't close your mouth!
issues.justification: In context the dentist's colleague is telling Shpak (who is working on a patient) not to let the patient close his mouth; the English is unclear without context and reads as a nonsensical command.

issues.source_quote: Закусывать надо! Быстрей!
issues.translation_quote: Should've had a bite with it! Faster!
issues.justification: Mistranslation of the imperative 'We must have a snack! Hurry!' into a past regret; the meaning is distorted.

issues.source_quote: Это - приятель Антона Семеновича Шпака. Ой, дурак! Надежа-царь говорит, что я - князь Милославский.
issues.translation_quote: Our hope the Tsar says that I am Prince Miloslavsky.
issues.justification: Miloslavsky speaks in his own modern voice here (translating Ivan's address as 'hope-Tsar'); 'Our hope the Tsar' is awkward and the Russian 'Надежа-царь' is a folk epithet that is rendered clumsily and inconsistently ('our hope', 'Great Sovereign, our hope').

issues.source_quote: Ты куда звонить собрался? - В милицию! - Положь трубку!
issues.translation_quote: Put that phone down! ... Lay that phone down! ... Lay it down, I'm telling you!
issues.justification: The joke rests on Ivan using the dialect/incorrect 'ложи/положь' and Bunsha's confused repetition; the translation replaces the grammatical error comedy with archaic 'lay', losing the humour about non-standard form.

issues.source_quote: Антон Семенович, Вас! - Кто спрашивает? Какая-то женщина.
issues.translation_quote: This is a certain actress.
issues.justification: Fine; not an error.

issues.source_quote: Ты на что, царская морда, намекаешь?
issues.translation_quote: Shpak's lost a tape machine, the envoy's locket's not been seen.
issues.justification: The rhyme 'У Шпака - магнитофон, у посла - медальон' is lost, and 'tape machine' and 'locket' are inconsistent with earlier 'tape recorder' and 'knightly order'/'medallion', creating terminology inconsistency and losing the comic rhyme.

issues.source_quote: Я Вас прошу, заявите! Заявите, а то мы сами заявим.
issues.translation_quote: I'm asking you, register it! Register it, or we'll report it ourselves.
issues.justification: 'Заявить' means to report to the authorities; 'register it' is a mistranslation and then 'report it ourselves' sounds inconsistent.

issues.source_quote: Это - Милославский? ... Тамбовский волк тебе боярин!
issues.translation_quote: Boyar, my foot!
issues.justification: The idiom 'a Tambov wolf is your boyar' is a Russian cultural expression and the English works as an adaptation; acceptable. No issue.

issues.source_quote: Потом ему должны дать квартиру, если, конечно, он не врет. Наверное, врет!
issues.translation_quote: And then they're supposed to give him a flat, unless, of course, he's lying. He probably is!
issues.justification: Acceptable; no issue.

issues.source_quote: Профессион де фуа!
issues.translation_quote: Profession de foy!
issues.justification: The French 'profession de foi' is a play on 'professional duty' (профессиональная обязанность → 'профессион де фуа'), and the misspelling 'foy' plus lack of any cue means the intended pun and the speaker's pretension are not conveyed.

issues.source_quote: Тебя ж узнать нельзя! Ты что напялил-то на себя?
issues.translation_quote: Look at the state of you, eh?
issues.justification: 'Look at the state of you' is rendered here adequately; minor tonal.

issues.source_quote: Одну минуточку, передайте Зинаиде Михайловне
issues.translation_quote: Just a moment, tell Zinaida Mikhailovna that Rozalia Frantsevna said...
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Это не нам тили-тили, Это мы не трали-вали.
issues.translation_quote: This ain't our diddle-diddle, this wasn't in the syllabus.
issues.justification: The rhyming refrain from a popular Soviet song is turned into a non-rhyming, dialectal 'ain't' plus an invented 'syllabus' line unrelated to the source, which breaks the Bunsha-as-Soviet-bureaucrat voice and the humour.

issues.source_quote: Слушаюсь!
issues.translation_quote: As you command!
issues.justification: Over-formal for a modern-sounding Soviet servile reply; repeated rendering weakens Fedya's comic servility.

issues.source_quote: Рюриковичи мы. ... Вы - Тарапунька и Штепсель нашелся.
issues.translation_quote: Who're you two, Laurel and Hardy?
issues.justification: Tarapunka and Shtepsel are a Soviet comedy duo; replacing them with Laurel and Hardy is a legitimate domestication, so acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Вы что-то хотели чистосердечно признаться? ... Ваше благородие
issues.translation_quote: Your Excellency, have mercy... Your Honour
issues.justification: Titles vary ('Ваше сиятельство' vs 'Ваше благородие') and are given as 'Your Excellency' and 'Your Honour', but 'Ваше сиятельство' is the title for a prince (Your Grace/Serene Highness); using 'Excellency' loses the progressive joke on rank.

issues.source_quote: Это Вы мне говорите, "Да ты ведьма?!" - Честно признаться - да!
issues.translation_quote: - Art thou a witch?! ... To be honest - yes!
issues.justification: Acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Целую! Трогай!
issues.translation_quote: Drive on!
issues.justification: Acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Их давно ищу, но в суматохе дней нелегко, нелегко повстречаться с ней
issues.translation_quote: The only one, eternal, eternal
issues.justification: Song translation is serviceable; no issue.

issues.source_quote: Тебя еще судить за это будут, мерзавец!
issues.translation_quote: You'll be tried in court for this, you scoundrel!
issues.justification: Acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Я Вам как представитель общественности заявляю: прекратить!
issues.translation_quote: As a representative of the community, I hereby declare: cease and desist!
issues.justification: 'Cease and desist' is a legal formula that is out of place for a Soviet building manager; also 'Today you blew the fuses' loses the 'прекратить' brevity. Minor register mismatch.

issues.source_quote: Теряют люди друг друга, а потом не найдут никогда
issues.translation_quote: Dental clinic? Hello! Extension 3-62.
issues.justification: No issue.

issues.source_quote: Ей-богу! - Ловят? - Ха. Как поймают, Якина на кол посадить!
issues.translation_quote: Are they being pursued? - Ha. When they're caught, impale Yakin on a stake!
issues.justification: Acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Кемска волость
issues.translation_quote: Kemska volost ... Kem volost
issues.justification: Inconsistent rendering of the same toponym ('Kem' in earlier lines vs 'Kemska volost' and 'Kem volost'); minor terminology inconsistency. Also 'Der grosser König ... Tsar und velikiy knyaz' garbled German and Russian with 'Usarussa' is unmotivated.

issues.source_quote: Ну, пошли дела кой-как.
issues.translation_quote: A dog with the police promised to come!
issues.justification: The line 'Собака с милицией обещала прийти' (about a police dog) is garbled into 'A dog with the police', producing a meaningless statement.

issues.source_quote: Я брошу мужа, этого святого человека со всеми удобствами.
issues.translation_quote: all mod cons
issues.justification: The comic phrase 'со всеми удобствами' (a flat with all conveniences, used as a pun) is rendered as a stray 'all mod cons' which is awkward but conveys the joke partially.

issues.source_quote: какую-то кикимору, которую он хватает за руки
issues.translation_quote: some fright
issues.justification: 'Кикимора' is a folkloric hag, used as an insult for an unattractive woman; 'fright' is weak and loses the folkloric insult, though acceptable as an idiom.

issues.source_quote: Вы пережгли пробки, а завтра пережжете весь дом!
issues.translation_quote: Today you blew the fuses, tomorrow you'll burn down the building!
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Вы ко мне пришли с магнитофоном?
issues.translation_quote: Did you come to Shpak's with a tape recorder?
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Это сон какой-то! Минуточку! За чей счет этот банкет?
issues.translation_quote: This is some kind of dream! Just a moment! Who's paying for this banquet?
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Минутку! Интересное кино!
issues.translation_quote: Well, this is a fine picture!
issues.justification: 'Интересное кино' is an idiom for 'what's going on here!'; rendered as 'fine picture' it is unclear and unnatural in English.

issues.source_quote: Один раз царице! Почки один раз царице!
issues.translation_quote: One kidneys for the Tsarina!
issues.justification: Grammatical error ('One kidneys'), which in English reads as a mistake rather than a deliberate comic effect.

issues.source_quote: Марфа Васильевна я.
issues.translation_quote: Marfa Vasilievna am I.
issues.justification: Inverted syntax is unnatural for a sixteenth-century tsarina; the source is plain, and the Yoda-like inversion creates an unintended comic tone.
